edges.description: Endolymphatic hydrops and labyrinthine membrane distortion/rupture disrupt vestibular sensory epithelia, triggering recurrent attacks of vertigo.
Distension of the cochlear duct by endolymphatic hydrops impairs cochlear mechanics and hair cell function, causing fluctuating and progressive sensorineural hearing loss.
Cochlear hydrops and inner ear fluid imbalance cause aberrant cochlear sensory signaling perceived as tinnitus.

Endolymphatic hydrops is associated with aural pressure or fullness as a core symptom of Meniere's disease, although the intermediate sensory mechanisms linking inner-ear fluid distension to aural fullness remain incompletely defined.
Imbalance between endolymph secretion in the cochlear duct and reabsorption in the endolymphatic sac leads to endolymph accumulation and hydrops.
Proinflammatory cytokine signaling in the endolymphatic sac or spiral ligament promotes local inflammation and fluid dysregulation, leading to endolymphatic hydrops.
Loss of blood-labyrinth barrier integrity disrupts inner ear fluid balance and vascular permeability, contributing to endolymphatic hydrops.

nodes.description: Elevated inflammatory markers and autoantibodies have been found in some patients, suggesting that immune-mediated inner ear damage may contribute to disease pathogenesis in a subset of cases. Local (inner ear/endolymphatic sac) and systemic immune activation includes cytokine signaling and NF-κB pathway engagement. TWEAK-FN14 receptor signaling and dysregulated Fcγ receptor polymorphisms contribute to immune complex-mediated injury.

nodes.description: The blood-labyrinth barrier (BLB) maintains inner-ear homeostasis through tight junctions between endothelial cells and pericytes. In MD, increased vascular permeability and oxidative/nitrosative stress damage the BLB, leading to edema and epithelial dysfunction. Elevated iNOS and nitrotyrosine levels indicate oxidative stress-mediated cascading cellular injury.

nodes.description: Meniere's disease is characterized by distension of the endolymphatic space (endolymphatic hydrops) due to impaired reabsorption of endolymph or excess production. This results in rupture of the membranous labyrinth and mixing of endolymph and perilymph, leading to vestibular and cochlear dysfunction.

nodes.description: Abnormal regulation of fluid and ion homeostasis in the inner ear, particularly involving potassium transport in the stria vascularis and endolymphatic sac, contributes to endolymph accumulation and hydrops formation. Dysregulation of Na+/K+-ATPase, NKCC1, and K+ channels disrupts the electrochemical gradients required for normal endolymphatic fluid balance.
